item.title: [Breaking] Miners’ deaths: Probe panel cites overcrowding, extreme heat, dehydration as causes
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi The independent ministerial committee investigating the recent deaths of 33 persons in the custody of the Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) in Minna, Niger State, has unravelled the cause of death of the suspects. In the Executive Summary by the chairman of the Committee, Jonathan Kure, on Tuesday in Abuja, when he presented the report to the Minister of Interior, Hon. Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo, the committee cited the causes of death to include “overcrowding, unsuitable detention condition, failure of duty of care, inadequate supervision”. It added that “fatalities resulted from environmental asphyxia caused by prolonged confinement in a severely overcrowded cell aggravated by heat stress and dehydration”. According to the committee, the operation which led to the arrest of the suspects was without an “operational order” or approval from the national headquarters of the NSCDC. item.title: Bayern praise ‘humble’ Kane after Ballon d’Or win
item.description: Bayern Munich assistant coach Aaron Danks on Tuesday praised Harry Kane after his Ballon d’Or win, saying the striker will already be focused on scoring his “next goal”. Kane, 33, was awarded the prestigious honour in his hometown of London on Monday evening, breaking through to win the award for the first time. Englishman Danks, who is in the dugout while head coach Vincent Kompany recovers in hospital from a virus, said receiving the game’s highest individual award would not change the England captain’s mindset. “I’m really happy for him and proud of what he’s achieved. I know Harry and his full focus will now be on his next goal, his next performances, his next games,” Danks said at a press conference on Tuesday. “He’ll be straight back into that professional, humble mindset that got him to this level.” Kane had won several goalscoring honours and was runner-up in the Premier League and Champions League with Tottenham but did not break through for a first team trophy until after he moved to Bayern in 2023. Since arriving in Munich, Kane has won two Bundesliga titles and the German Cup, along with making the Champions League semi-finals in two of three seasons at Bayern. Danks said the former Spurs striker was finally getting the recognition he deserves. “I remember years ago when he was back home in England and everybody spoke about him not winning trophies, but if you looked at his career and what he was achieving, he was having a fantastic career. “He was taking the England team to European finals, he was taking Tottenham to Champions League finals. “Maybe he wasn’t getting the recognition in terms of trophies that he deserved, but those things are coming now for him.” Kane and the remaining Bayern contingent who went to London for the ceremony will return to Munich later on Tuesday ahead of Wednesday’s German Cup match against second-tier Magdeburg. “They’re due back at lunchtime today. He’ll train, practice this afternoon and be available for tomorrow… Our full focus is on the game tomorrow,” Danks said. Danks also said he had visited Kompany in hospital and revealed the manager, who was rushed to hospital on Friday after collapsing on the training pitch, was improving. “He’s in good spirits. It looks like every day he’s getting better. There’s no major updates in terms of diagnosis or a return to work, it’s very calm, let him rest, let him recover.” After seven games, Bayern sit top of the Bundesliga, level on points but ahead on goal difference from Borussia Dortmund, with the two sides facing off in Munich on Saturday. item.title: Rivers Police nab 5 kidnappers who lure victims through dating sites
item.description: By Davies Iheamnachor Operatives of the Rivers State Police Command have arrested five kidnappers who specialise in luring their victims through online dating sites. The operatives also rescued a female victim in the custody of the abductors who was lured into Port Harcourt through the online platform. The Public Relations Officer of the Command, Blessing Agabe, an Assistant Superintendent of Police, in a statement in Port Harcourt, Tuesday, said the suspects were tracked following intelligence. Agabe stated that the victim, Chinyere, came in from Delta State for a visit and was kidnapped along Igwuruta-Etche Road in Ikwerre Local Government Area of Rivers State. She said: “The Rivers State Police Command has arrested five suspected kidnappers allegedly involved in the abduction of a 24-year-old woman, one Chinyere, along the Igwuruta, Etche Road in Rivers State. “On October 4, 2026, at about 0900 hours, the Command received a complaint that one Chinyere had been kidnapped. The victim had reportedly travelled from Delta State to Port Harcourt on October 3, 2026, to visit a friend when she was abducted along the Igwirita–Etche Road. “Following the directives of the Commissioner of Police, Rivers State Police Command, CP Olugbenga A. Adepoju, psc, mnips, fcai, Upon receipt of the complaint, the operatives of the Command Violent Crime Response Unit (VCRU) Diobu immediately swung into action and arrested the perpetrators of this crime.” Agabe said that the suspects during investigation confessed to the crime, advising members of the public to be careful of dating platforms. She said: “During investigation, the suspects confessed to their involvement in the kidnapping and disclosed information about other kidnapping incidents within Igwuruta and Etche. They further disclosed that they lured victims from within and outside Port Harcourt through online dating sites before abducting them.” The post Rivers Police nab 5 kidnappers who lure victims through dating sites appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Reps move to halt school fee hikes, probe 100% increases in public institutions
item.description: By Gift ChapiOdekina, Abuja The House of Representatives has urged the Federal Government to suspend recent increases in school fees by public tertiary institutions across the country, warning that the hikes could undermine the objectives of the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND). The House also mandated its committees on University Education, Federal Polytechnics and Higher Technical Education, and Federal Colleges of Education to investigate the extent and justification for the fee increases. The resolutions followed a motion sponsored by Hon. Ifeoluwa Ehindero, who expressed concern that some public universities, polytechnics and colleges of education had increased their fees and other mandatory charges by more than 100 per cent. The lawmaker noted that the increases were implemented without broad consultation or adequate consideration of the prevailing economic realities facing Nigerian families. According to the motion, education remains a cornerstone of national development and a fundamental objective of state policy under Section 18 of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which requires government to ensure equal and adequate educational opportunities at all levels. The House observed that NELFUND was established by the Federal Government to provide interest-free loans to students in need, enabling them to pursue tertiary education without financial barriers. However, it expressed concern that arbitrary or sudden increases in school fees could undermine the sustainability and effectiveness of the loan scheme, which was designed around existing tuition benchmarks and institutional cost structures. The lawmakers warned that unchecked increases could create disparities in the allocation of education loans and further disadvantage students from low-income households. They also cautioned that the development could lead to increased student dropouts, unrest on campuses and a loss of public confidence in the government’s commitment to affordable education. To address the situation, the House urged the Federal Government to increase financial subventions to public tertiary institutions to reduce their dependence on internally generated revenue through student charges. It also called on the Federal Ministry of Education and the National Universities Commission to engage the managements of public tertiary institutions on suspending the fee increases and conducting a comprehensive review of tuition structures in line with current economic realities. The House further directed the relevant committees to investigate the circumstances surrounding the increases and establish whether the adjustments were justified. The proposed intervention is aimed at protecting access to higher education and ensuring that rising institutional charges do not defeat the objectives of NELFUND, particularly for students from financially disadvantaged backgrounds. item.title: IPOB declares total boycott of APC over delays in listing Nnamdi Kanu’s appeal
item.description: . Accuses FG of frustrating hearing, demands leader’s release By Steve Oko The Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) has declared a total political boycott of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC), accusing the Federal Government of frustrating the appeal of its detained leader, Nnamdi Kanu, against his conviction. The pro -Biafra movement said it would boycott APC’s rallies and reject its insignia until Kanu’s appeal is listed for hearing, declaring: “No listing, no participation.” In a statement issued by its Media and Publicity Secretary, Emma Powerful, IPOB accused the government of failing to facilitate the hearing of the appeal against the November 20, 2025 judgment, alleging that the case remained unlisted and that the government had yet to file its respondent’s brief. The group argued that the appeal raised fundamental constitutional questions concerning Kanu’s conviction under a law it claims had been repealed. It urged the relevant authorities to ensure that the appeal proceeds, insisting that the courts should determine the legal issues rather than allow procedural delays to persist. IPOB also raised concerns over what it described as the disappearance of the court file relating to Kanu’s alleged 14-month detention without trial following his discharge by the Court of Appeal on October 13, 2022. The group called for the restoration of the file and accused the authorities of frustrating efforts to secure judicial redress. Beyond Kanu’s legal battle, IPOB accused the Federal Government of applying double standards in its security operations, alleging that military operations, arrests and detentions targeted at people in the South-East contrasted with the handling of armed groups in other parts of the country. The group also criticised former Ebonyi State Governor and Minister of Works, David Umahi, over his role in the 2017 decision by South-East governors to proscribe IPOB, alleging that the move contributed to subsequent security crackdowns in the region. It further warned South-East politicians aligned with the APC against what it described as sacrificing the interests of the Igbo people for political benefits. IPOB, however, directed its supporters to pursue the boycott peacefully, warning against harassment or threats against citizens because of their political affiliations. Reiterating its position, the group demanded Kanu’s immediate and unconditional release, the listing of his appeal and the restoration of the allegedly missing court file. The APC and the Federal Government had yet to respond to the allegations contained in the statement as of the time of filing this report. item.title: ‘We no longer sleep with two eyes closed’ — Nasarawa lawmaker laments kidnappings
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia Member representing the Lafia Central constituency at the Nasarawa State House of Assembly, Hon. Solomon Yakubu Akwashiki, has said that the people of his constituency cannot longer sleep with their two eyes closed due to the frequent abduction of the people in the constituency. The lawmaker, while raising the issue on the floor of the House on Tuesday as a matter of public interest, urged the security agencies and the state government to be more committed to protecting the lives and property of its citizens. He said, “Mr Speaker and my honourable colleagues, I rise on a matter of frequent kidnapping in my constituency. “Yesterday, in Agyaragu Lafia, two people were kidnapped. Days back, in Agunji Lafia, people were kidnapped. “As I am talking, the two people kidnapped yesterday are in the hands of the kidnappers, and they are demanding ransom. “Security agencies and the state government should rise up to curtail the rate of kidnapping and other forms of insecurity in my constituency,” he appealed. Reacting to the alarm over a fresh resurgence of kidnapping incidents across the State, the Speaker of the House, Dr Danladi Jatau, said that the State capital and some parts of the State are experiencing frequent abductions that have caused fear and economic setbacks to the State. The speaker appreciated the mover of the motion and other colleagues for their positive contributions on the issue. “The resolution of the House is to the effect that we urge His Excellency, Gov. Abdullahi Sule, to direct all security agencies, the Commissioner of Police, and the DSS and NSCDC to beam their satellites across the state to curtail the rate of kidnapping. “All hands must be on deck, especially Chiefs and Village Heads, in collaboration with Vigilantes to identify strange people in their communities,” he said. The Speaker directed the Clerk of the House to communicate the House resolution to Gov. Sule for his necessary action. Also contributing, Hon. Esson Mairiga Esq, Hon. Onarigu Onah Kana, Hon. Ibrahim Abdullahi Sa’ad, Hon. Suleiman Yakubu Azara, Rt Hon. Abel Yakubu Bala and Hon. Larry Ven-Bawa supported the motion and called on the state government to beef up security across the state in order to curtail the rate of kidnapping in the state. They lamented how kidnapping is affecting the lives of their people negatively. The lawmakers, however, appreciated the efforts of Gov. Sule in terms of security but urged him and security agencies to be more committed to tackling the rate of kidnapping across the state. The lawmakers collectively called on security agencies to intensify operations. They called on both the federal and state governments to purchase sophisticated weapons via technology to tackle insecurity in the state. item.title: Police confirm man, teenager swept away by flood in Aba
item.description: By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Abia State Police Command has confirmed that a man who attempted to rescue a teenage girl from a water-filled ditch at Faulks Road, Aba, was swept away alongside the girl during Sunday’s downpour. The Police Public Relations Officer, Maureen Chinaka, disclosed this while responding to Vanguard inquiries, confirming that the incident occurred around the popular Ukwu Mango area of the commercial city. Chinaka said the tragedy happened near an ongoing construction site where an uncovered ditch had filled with rainwater. According to her, the teenage girl was passing through the area when she reportedly hit a stone and fell into the ditch. An adult who witnessed the incident reportedly plunged into the water in an attempt to rescue her, but both were swept away. “Unfortunately, we have not been able to see them. The police are aware, and the matter has been reported. Efforts are in place to see how they can be rescued,” Chinaka said. She confirmed that the two victims had yet to be found as search efforts continued. Asked whether the construction company responsible for the site would face possible charges over negligence, the police spokesperson said investigations were on-going. The tragedy has raised concerns about the safety of construction sites during heavy rainfall, particularly where excavations and drainage channels are left uncovered and become submerged in floodwater. Aba’s flat terrain makes parts of the commercial city vulnerable to flooding during heavy downpours, increasing the risks posed by waterlogged roads, open drains and excavations. item.title: Nigeria’s economic crisis predates Tinubu, says ex-minister, Ikoh
item.description: By Steve Oko Former Minister of State for Science and Technology and Abia State Coordinator of Renewed Hope Ambassadors, Chief Henry Ikechukwu Ikoh, has said Nigeria’s economic crisis predates President Bola Tinubu’s administration, urging Nigerians to assess the government’s reforms against the country’s longstanding structural challenges. Ikoh, who made the submission in a statement by his media aide, Smart Anthony Ogbonna, said Nigeria’s overdependence on crude oil, inadequate industrial diversification, inflation and inconsistent economic policies had contributed to decades of economic difficulties. He noted that Tinubu inherited these challenges in May 2023 and introduced reforms, including petrol subsidy removal and foreign exchange market adjustments, to address fiscal imbalances and establish a more sustainable economy. While acknowledging the hardships caused by the measures, Ikoh argued that their success should ultimately be measured by their impact on employment, food affordability, investment and citizens’ purchasing power. He called for sustained reforms, increased agricultural and industrial production, infrastructure development and effective policy implementation to translate macroeconomic gains into tangible improvements in living standards. The Abia APC chieftain expressed confidence that a second term for Tinubu would consolidate the ongoing reforms, create jobs, attract investment and accelerate economic recovery. He urged Nigerians to support the continuation of the administration’s Renewed Hope Agenda, arguing that policy consistency would provide an opportunity to deepen reforms and expand economic opportunities. item.title: Tinubu approves 500,000 solar lights for S’East households — Deputy Speaker, Kalu
item.description: By Steve Oko Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, has said President Bola Tinubu has approved the provision of 500,000 solar-powered lights for rural households in the South-East. Kalu disclosed this at the flag-off of the Renewed Hope Light-Up initiative, during which 26 transformers and 10,000 solar-powered lights and fans were distributed to communities in Bende Federal Constituency, Abia State. He said 42,000 households in the constituency had been earmarked to benefit from the initiative, with the first batch of 10,000 solar-powered lights and fans expected to be delivered within two weeks. According to him, 1,000 units had already been distributed as a pilot scheme, with representatives from the federal constituency’s wards confirming their functionality. Kalu said the initiative was designed to make the benefits of the Renewed Hope Agenda tangible to rural residents, particularly households that had struggled with unreliable electricity supply. He described the planned provision of solar-powered lights to 42,000 households in a single federal constituency as unprecedented, adding that the initiative would help improve access to electricity in underserved communities. The lawmaker representing Bende South Constituency in the Abia State House of Assembly, Emmanuel Ndubuisi, described the intervention as significant, noting that some communities had been without electricity for about two years following transformer failures. A representative of the project contractor, Solar Systems Nigeria, Peter Oko, said the initiative would also provide opportunities for youth training and empowerment. He assured beneficiaries of the company’s commitment to delivering quality and reliable services. Earlier, Director-General of the Ben Kalu Campaign Council, Emma Trump Eke, described the intervention as a landmark project for Bende Federal Constituency. item.title: China brands drop Mbappe for ‘offending national sentiments’
item.description: Kylian Mbappe was dropped on Tuesday by major Chinese brands after a video circulated of the Real Madrid and France superstar apparently joking about Mao Zedong. There were also signs of broader repercussions, with state-run The Paper reporting that public television was suspending broadcasts of matches from Spain’s La Liga. The offending video shows Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen involving him was of his face photo-shopped onto that of “some guy — I think he’s a Chinese dictator”. This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao, one of several using the footballer’s face and other historical figures. The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check. In China, jokes about Mao, the country’s founding leader who died in 1976 — and whose drastic policies are also blamed by historians for mass starvation and millions of deaths — remain taboo. Beverage giant Dongpeng, which during this year’s World Cup ran adverts with AI-generated images of Mbappe consuming its sports drink, said it was terminating all cooperation with the France captain. “Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments,” Dongpeng said in a statement. Mengniu, China’s largest dairy producer, and cheesemaker Milkground also said that they were cutting ties with Mbappe, who until now was hugely popular among Chinese fans with millions of followers on social media. Mbappe is fondly nicknamed “Guigui”, the Chinese translation of “Turtle”, due to his popularity as a character in a Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles meme. “Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe” was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo with 430 million views. One Weibo user said that the “extremely serious wrong remarks… crossed the red line”. Others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe’s image from their energy drink bottles. Dongqiudi, one of China’s biggest online football outlets, said in a statement on Monday evening that Mbappe’s remarks were “offensive to China and the Chinese people”. – Furore – In an interview with French sports newspaper L’Equipe, the 27-year-old Mbappe in September addressed a previous meme depicting him as a military dictator. “There’s a part of it that’s funny… but there is another part that’s a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history,” he said. Asked on Tuesday about the controversy, China’s foreign ministry said that it was aware of the reports. “Words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people will naturally be met with unanimous rejection from all sectors of Chinese society,” spokesman Guo Jiakun told a regular briefing. State media outlet The Paper cited sources at the state broadcaster saying that CCTV has suspended all broadcasts of La Liga matches, and that all advertisements involving Mbappe have also been removed. item.title: Ballon d’Or: Barcelona star honours late Nigerian mother after winning Young talent award
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Barcelona and Spain forward Vicky López has paid an emotional tribute to her late Nigerian mother, Joy Felix, after winning the Women’s Young Player of the Year award at the 2026 Ballon d’Or ceremony on Monday. The 20-year-old attacking midfielder dedicated the honour to her mother, who died when she was 11, saying she continued to feel her presence despite her absence. “Mum, although you can’t be with me physically, I feel your presence every day. Everything I’ve achieved I owe to you, so thank you for teaching me never to give up,” López said. “Thank you to everyone in football and let’s keep making this sport better.” The Barcelona star, whose father is Spanish and mother Nigerian, was born in 2006 in Vallecas, a working-class neighbourhood in Madrid. Her journey in football began at an early age, playing in the streets with her older brother, Jesus, when she was just four. Spanish football journalist Irati Vidal told BBC Sport that López’s style was heavily influenced by street football, where she developed the flair, agility and speed that have become part of her game. “Vicky learned her craft on the streets of Vallecas, her style is very street-influenced,” Vidal said. “She used to play for fun while admiring and trying to copy Neymar’s dribbles.” López’s latest recognition follows an impressive 2025-26 campaign in which Barcelona won Liga F, the Copa de la Reina, the Supercopa de España and the UEFA Women’s Champions League. The award was her second consecutive Women’s Young Player of the Year honour, having also won the inaugural edition in 2025. Beyond her club achievements, López has set her sights on representing Spain at the 2027 FIFA Women’s World Cup in Brazil. “I think wearing the Spain shirt is a dream that all girls who play football have,” she told Antena 3 Deportes. “For me, winning a World Cup with Spain would be one of the greatest achievements.” Her ambition is also tied to the memory of her mother, whom she has described as a major source of motivation. “For me, my mother is everything. A goal I have in life is to make her proud.” The post Ballon d’Or: Barcelona star honours late Nigerian mother after winning Young talent award appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigerian newspapers review: [NESG] We’re rewriting Nigeria’s story of underperformance – Tinubu
item.description: In today’s Nigerian newspapers review programme, Today in the News, Vanguard leads with President Bola Tinubu saying at the 32nd Nigerian Economic Summit Group (NESG) in Abuja that his administration is rewriting Nigeria’s decades-long story of economic underperformance through far-reaching reforms designed to dismantle structural barriers, unlock the nation’s enormous potential and deliver jobs, productivity and shared prosperity. Another headline features the World Health Organisation (WHO) Regional Director for Africa, Dr Mohamed Janabi, saying Nigeria currently has no Ebola cases following the medical evacuation of the patient and her husband to Switzerland. Vanguard also reports that an investigator with the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), Yakubu Ibrahim, on Monday, told a Federal High Court in Abuja that both the University of Nigeria (UNN) and the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) disowned the degree and discharge certificates presented by former Minister of Innovation, Science and Technology, Uche Nnaji, to the Senate for his ministerial screening in 2023. Moving to another newspaper, The Guardian reports that despite 25 State Houses of Assembly endorsing the State Police Bill, persistent fears over political interference, human rights violations and weak accountability have raised questions about whether the proposed safeguards can protect citizens from abuse or remain largely theoretical. The Punch leads with organised labour looking forward to its next action after a crucial meeting with the Federal Government on Tuesday, with the Nigeria Labour Congress and Trade Union Congress demanding concrete proposals on petrol prices, wage negotiations and other unresolved workers’ welfare issues amid the threat of nationwide industrial action. Lastly, Daily Trust reports that the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, said some Nigerians spend as much as 120 per cent of their income on food, forcing them to borrow money or rely on relatives to survive. item.title: Houthi official says Egypt’s military support for Saudi declaration of war
item.description: A Houthi official said Tuesday that the Egyptian parliament’s decision to authorise military support for Saudi Arabia to defend against the Iran-backed group’s attacks was a declaration of war. The comment was part of a long statement reacting to a Monday visit to Tehran by the Saudi defence minister, alongside Pakistan’s army chief and Turkey’s intelligence chief, in a bid to de-escalate tensions in the Middle East war. “It is truly remarkable that while these people go to discuss what they call ‘peace in the region’, Egypt and its parliament declare support for the so-called defence of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, and in doing so, declare war against the Republic of Yemen,” said Mohammed Ali al-Houthi, a member of the Houthis’ political bureau, in a Telegram post. Saudi Defence Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan’s army chief General Asim Munir and Turkey’s intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin attended the talks with Mohsen Rezaei, head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council. They also met Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian. Iran, Pakistan and Turkey recently signed a Nato-style defence pact in Mecca that says an attack on one country is to be considered an attack on all three. But since the Houthis ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia earlier this month, the two other countries have not announced any strikes on the group. Al-Houthi said the pact was “a clear and blatant act of aggression against the Islamic Republic of Iran”, adding that the group was “not afraid of any alliance that may be formed”. In July, Yemen’s conflict flared up again as a fragile 2022 truce fell apart after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen’s capital Sanaa, in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks. The Houthis then declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before launching a major offensive in September in which they seized Yemeni government-held territory along the Red Sea coast. In response, the Houthis have reported frequent Saudi strikes targeting areas under their control. In October, the Houthis ramped up their attacks on Saudi Arabia, forcing the cancellation of flagship events and a shutdown of Riyadh airport for two weeks. item.title: DSS arraigns man over fake Tinubu letter to US president
item.description: The Department of State Services (DSS) has filed a three-count charge bordering on cybercrime and defamation against a Kaduna man accused of circulating a fake letter purportedly written by President Bola Tinubu to the President of the United States. The suspect, Mubarak Abdullahi, also known as Sardaunan Samari, was arrested on September 28 after allegedly sharing the document on his Facebook page with the caption, “ATIKU IS COMING.” President Tinubu’s Special Adviser on Information and Strategy, Bayo Onanuga, disclosed this in a post on X late Monday, saying Abdullahi had been arraigned before Chief Magistrate Court No. 10, Kabala Doki, Kaduna. The tweet read, “An avowed supporter of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar now faces trial in Kaduna for circulating a document purportedly written by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to the President of the United States of America. “The suspect, Mubarak Abdullahi (aka Sardaunan Samari), was arrested on 28 September for sharing the fake document on his Facebook page with the caption “ATIKU IS COMING.” “Mubarak admitted to investigators that he shared the fake document and apologised for his actions. The contrition was not enough. “The DSS arraigned him before Chief Magistrate Court No. 10, Kabala Doki, Kaduna, which ordered his remand at the Nigerian Correctional Centre, Kaduna,” adding that the agency “has filed a three-count charge bordering on cybercrime and defamation against him at the Federal High Court, Kaduna.” Onanuga, however, said the DSS would continue to demonstrate its ability to identify people involved in circulating what he described as misleading information online. Meanwhile, human rights activist and presidential candidate of the African Action Congress (AAC) Omoyele Sowore criticised the arrest, accusing the DSS of being used to suppress dissent. In a post on X on Tuesday, Sowore questioned the agency’s involvement in the case and described the arrest as an attempt to silence a citizen over an online post. “How low will you go, #OfficialAPCNg and the #officialABAT regime? How on earth do you reduce a national security agency like the #OfficialDSSNG to a mere vacuum cleaner, deployed to sweep up dissenting voices in your inordinate ambition to subdue every citizen simply because you are afraid to face the Nigerian people and account for your disastrous reign?” he wrote. Sowore added, “Arresting a hapless citizen for posting a document online – sad! Shame on all of you! A day of reckoning is coming, when you too will be held accountable for your actions. That day is coming sooner than you think. Very soon!” Neither Atiku nor his media aide, Phrank Shaibu, had publicly reacted to the development as of the time of writing. item.title: EKO HOTELS AT 50: THE NIGHT AFRICAN HOSPITALITY STOPPED ASKING FOR A SEAT AT THE GLOBAL TABLE
item.description: The Legacy Gala & Awards night: Fifty Years of Building More Than a Hotel. Fifty Years of Building a Nation’s Hospitality Identity. In LAGOS, NIGERIA, 2nd of OCTOBER 2026 was written in the sands of time, because some hotels are built to accommodate history. Others are built to make it. For fifty years, Eko Hotels & Suites has done both. Beneath the lights of an extraordinary golden jubilee celebration, one of Africa’s most recognisable hospitality institutions made a statement that extended far beyond the walls of the magnificent Eko Convention Centre. Africa does not lack the capacity to deliver world-class excellence. What it needs are more institutions courageous enough to demonstrate it. The occasion was The Legacy Gala & Awards night, the grand celebration marking fifty years of Eko Hotels & Suites. An evening of African grandeur, international entertainment, cultural pride, distinguished personalities and extraordinary hospitality. But to describe it simply as a glamorous anniversary celebration would be to misunderstand its significance. This was not merely a party. It was fifty years of enterprise taking a bow. Fifty years of memories finding their voices. Fifty years of an institution reminding a continent that excellence is not foreign to Africa. And for one unforgettable evening, history took attendance. A HOTEL BECAME PART OF A NATION’S STORY There are buildings that occupy space, and there are institutions that occupy memory. Eko Hotels & Suites belongs to the latter. Across five decades, its corridors have welcomed presidents and policymakers, entrepreneurs and entertainers, diplomats and dreamers, international visitors and generations of Nigerian families. Within its halls, businesses have been negotiated, friendships formed, cultures celebrated, careers launched and milestones immortalised. For many, Eko Hotels is where Lagos welcomes the world. For others, it is where the world first encounters the warmth, ambition, sophistication and extraordinary possibilities of Lagos. Yet perhaps its greatest achievement is not simply that it has remained standing for fifty years. It is that it has remained RELEVANT. In a world where brands disappear as quickly as trends emerge, longevity is an achievement. But longevity accompanied by reinvention is leadership. Eko Hotels has consistently demonstrated that hospitality must evolve beyond accommodation. It must become an experience. A cultural encounter. An economic opportunity. A reason to travel. A reason to return. Because the greatest hotels do not merely sell rooms. They give destinations a reputation worth travelling for. item.title: Gunmen kill seven in Plateau community
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen on Monday night stormed Georo community in Jos South Local Government Area of Plateau State, killing seven persons in an attack that threw residents into panic. The attackers, who invaded the community at about 10:20pm, reportedly opened fire sporadically, killing some persons in their shops and others at a local restaurant. A member of the community, Mr Bot Silas, who confirmed the incident, said, “The gunmen stormed the community at about 10:20pm and started shooting sporadically.” Silas said, “Some of the victims were killed in their shops, while others were attacked at a local restaurant where food was being prepared.” He added, “Seven persons were killed in the attack, and the incident caused serious panic among residents of the community.” Silas said, “The attackers came at night and started shooting, forcing residents to scamper for safety.” Reacting to the incident, spokesman of the Berom Youth Moulders Association, BYM, Rwang Tengwong, condemned the attack and described it as unacceptable. Tengwong said, “The killing of innocent people in Georo is condemnable and must not be allowed to continue.” “I call on the relevant security agencies to intensify efforts to protect communities and apprehend those responsible for the attack.” Tengwong added, “We call on the relevant security agencies to investigate the incident, bring the perpetrators to justice and ensure that residents can live and carry out their legitimate activities without fear.” The post Gunmen kill seven in Plateau community appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: US midterms: Five issues shaping the vote
item.description: Americans voting in the November 3 midterm elections will decide who controls Congress for the final two years of Donald Trump’s presidency, along with dozens of governorships and thousands of state offices. The campaign is playing out against an unusually combustible mix of economic anxiety, war, immigration battles, corruption concerns and unease over rapidly expanding artificial intelligence. Polls asking voters about priorities use different methodologies, but they broadly agree on the dominance of pocketbook concerns. An October Pew survey found economic issues easily topped voters’ worries, while a September Emerson poll put the Iran war, jobs, tariffs, gas prices, immigration and AI regulation among the most important factors in voting decisions. Here are five issues shaping the midterms: – It’s the economy – Affordability remains issue number one. Inflation was running at 3.7 percent in September, but the political problem goes beyond the headline rate, with voters paying more for gasoline, housing, electricity, groceries and borrowing. Pew found that 65 percent of Americans see Trump’s economic policies as hurtful to the economy. Another survey, from the Joseph Rainey Center for Public Policy, found 57 percent placing groceries, gas or utilities among their top three issues. Trump’s tariffs feed directly into the debate, with opponents blaming them for higher costs while the administration argues they protect American industry and raise revenue. – Iran war – A foreign war has become a domestic pocketbook issue. The conflict with Iran, underway since February, has driven energy costs higher and become deeply unpopular. Emerson’s September survey rated the Iran war the single most important issue among those it tested, while Reuters/Ipsos found only 34 percent approving of Trump’s handling of the conflict. Republican candidates in several competitive races have called for the fighting to end, and four Republican senators joined Democrats in a September vote seeking to rein it in. – Immigration – The strength of Trump’s signature political talking point has become more complicated. The president returned to office promising mass deportations, but support has eroded following controversy over deaths during arrests and detention, and aggressive ICE operations. Reuters/Ipsos found 55 percent disapproved of Trump’s handling of immigration. Marist, meanwhile, found Democrats and Republicans essentially level on which party voters trusted more on the issue — a striking change from the clear Republican advantage of 2024. The shift is particularly notable among Latinos. A survey across competitive House districts found 62 percent of Latino voters disapproved of the administration’s deportation and immigration enforcement. – Trump, money and power – The president himself is an issue — including how he uses the office.
